messages:
jamie (product): Hey folks — kicking off the pricing/usage Q&A thread. Post short questions about rate limits, quota/credit behavior, or what happens when customers change tiers. We'll field live answers. :wave:

leah (support): Quick one — if a customer upgrades from Starter -> Pro mid-month, do their unused Starter credits get applied to Pro or prorated?
sara (finance): Short answer: we prorate monetary charges, not credit buckets. Unused Starter credit units are not automatically converted. We do offer manual migrations for enterprise seats — ping billing for exceptions.

mike (eng): To add technical detail: credits are an application-layer concept for hosted plans. When you move plans the credit_balance field stays with the account but pricing per-unit changes. No automatic top-ups or conversions.

raj (sre): Another related question we've seen — during region failover will rate limits reset or carry over? For Hosted we have regional rate boundaries; failover will land in a different region and the per-region counters may be separate, so you can see temporary double-counting of allowed units. We try to avoid giving customers extra quota during failover, but in practice you might get brief capacity spikes.

jamie (product): Thanks — follow-up: do we provide a grace window for customers who hit a credit cliff after a deploy/bug?
sara (finance): We have a 72-hour soft-grace for certain paying tiers (e.g., annual commitments) — this is policy, not automatic for trial/free tiers. Support can approve 1-off grace extensions.

leah (support): Example customer question we've had: 'I got 429s after a sudden ramp despite being under plan limits.' Is that just rate-limiter behavior?
mike (eng): Usually 429s mean you hit a per-tenant concurrency or per-route token/sec cap. If it's a sudden spike we'll recommend enabling burst-capacity for Dedicated or moving to a higher rate_limit band for Hosted. Check /metrics for request_per_min and token_per_sec spikes.

mike (eng): Quick diagnostic snippet you can paste into a ticket to show headers:
```
curl -I https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "x-rd-usage: tokens=2450"
```
If the response includes `x-rd-rate-limit: 100` and `x-rd-rate-remaining: 0` that's a clear 429 cause.

eden (legal): Small note on policy: we can't promise credits/transfers as a legal entitlement unless the contract explicitly states it. For enterprise deals, include explicit credit migration language.

jamie (product): Action items: 1) Mike to add a short FAQ section about tier transitions and credit behavior to the docs. 2) Sara to share a one-pager on grace windows and finance exceptions. 3) Leah to add a ticket template for requests to migrate credits.

mike (eng): I'll update docs: https://redwood.com/docs/usage-migration (draft) — will ping when live.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: docs/usage-migration -> prod @ 1751240200

raj (sre): One more: rate-limit exemptions during incidents — we keep some limited emergency overrides but they require an Ops-runbook step and approval from oncall + product. Not an automated bypass.

leah (support): Thanks team — I'll consolidate answers into a KB and link back to this thread. :memo:

jamie (product): Great, thanks everyone. If we missed specific customer scenarios drop them here or open a ticket and tag me. :+1:
